overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the bootstrap and policy. The widest surface in the estate by omission count: 37 released attributes and four declared groupings over unifi.Network. Of its 263 SDK fields, 196 are omitted, 47 are bound one to one, and 20 are related to an attribute through one of seven claims -- counted from the mapping report rather than estimated, because the first version of this entry said 223 omitted and was simply wrong. THE OMISSION SET IS DERIVED AND VERIFIED, NOT REVIEWED. A field is omitted if and only if the released schema does not expose it, so cmd/policy-scaffold derives the set from the contract rather than choosing it. Exactly-once accounting refuses an unclassified field, so a MISSING omission cannot pass; and a WRONG one cannot either, because the built schema would then lack an attribute the baseline has and the projection referee would name it. The 196 lines were not hand-read, and hand-reading them would not have added a correctness guarantee -- it would answer a different question, whether a field OUGHT to be exposed that the released schema does not expose either, which is a pre-existing gap in the provider rather than a migration defect. What this width genuinely costs is that the policy is unreadable in review. SEVEN CLAIMS. vlan relates one released number to the observed vlan AND vlan_enabled, which the provider sets from whether vlan was configured at all. purpose and third_party_gateway are TWO released attributes over ONE observed purpose: the configured purpose is honoured and then overwritten to vlan-only when third_party_gateway is true, and on read both are computed from the one field. Four more distribute a released list positionally into numbered slots -- dhcp_guarding.servers into three, dhcp_server.dns_servers and dhcp_v6_server.dns_servers into four each, and dhcp_server.wins over an enable flag and two slots -- and dhcp_server.boot groups three flat fields. Their to_api and from_api halves differ: the writes are positional and the reads compact, so a value moves slot on a round trip, and dhcp_guarding.servers does not clear the slots it does not use while dhcp_server.dns_servers does. ipv6_aliases is the surface's trap. The SDK carries a field of that name AND the released schema carries an attribute of that name, and THEY ARE NOT CONNECTED: the write is commented out as not available in the API, and the read sets the attribute to null unconditionally. Binding them by name is exactly the static_route failure. The SDK field is omitted and the attribute is provider-owned, which preserves an attribute that accepts configuration and discards it -- a defect, but not one a migration may fix. Six behaviours inside dhcp_server.boot and dhcp_server.wins were transcribed by hand: both are claimed members, whose nested objects are hand-authored, so cmd/schema-behaviour names them rather than writing them. The behaviour inventory is what confirms they survived. Admission waits on a campaign run.
